payload.reason: Characterize the physical event behind the line_green clamp-effort spike (191 vs 170 threshold) during final seating move

payload.explanation: Monitor effort_line_green (threshold invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous, le 170, from raw_spec.limits.max_clamp_effort for line_green) fired at trigger_wall_ns=1792027021740214800 with instantaneous finger_joint effort 191.192, exceeding the object's tolerated 170. get_evidence on joint_states/finger_joint over the surrounding window shows effort climbing smoothly from a steady ~8.9 baseline (normal hold) starting ~1792027020886749000, through 85, 114, 143, peaking 191.19, then oscillating 130-180 for several seconds, while finger_joint position barely changed (0.5404->0.5382, i.e. the gripper was not closing further or slipping open) -- this pattern is resistance against a rigid obstruction, not a slip or a stronger intentional grip. This occurred during the final move_grasp_center_to_pose into the seating pose at the base1 fixture (place_line_green begin_step named line_green, u_brown, u_orange as co-located parts). A look() at the scene afterward shows the gripper positioned directly over the base1 cross-slot with line_green pressed down into it. The mechanism is judged to be line_green's insertion into the base1 slot encountering mechanical resistance (misalignment or tight fit against the slot/neighboring parts), transmitted back through the held part as clamp force exceeding tolerance, rather than an intentional over-grip or a slip. This is a genuine clamp-effort invariant violation regardless of mechanism.

Monitor slip_line_green (relative_frame, tcp<->line_green, max_delta_m 0.02 from raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m, instruction-level in-hand-slippage requirement, no contract clause_id) fired at trigger_wall_ns=1792027022512411600 with a 0.021328 m departure from the arm-time reference, just over the 0.02 m tolerance. This falls in the same window as the clamp-effort spike recorded moments earlier in this step (peak 191.19 at ~1792027021740214800): get_evidence on the tcp frame over this window shows the TCP descending smoothly (z from 0.1542 to 0.1327 m) with no discontinuity, i.e. the commanded motion itself was a normal, continuous lowering into the seating pose, not a jerk or collision of the arm. finger_joint position over the same window barely changed (0.5404 rad at grasp to 0.5382-0.5386 rad here), ruling out a width change as the cause of the apparent offset per the monitor's own caveat. Taken together with the concurrent effort spike, the most likely physical event is that line_green met resistance seating into the base1 slot and shifted marginally within the gripper's grasp under that reaction force -- a small real slip, not a mis-arming or re-grip artifact. It is a narrow violation (6.6% over tolerance) but the invariant is binary and the evidence shows a genuine in-hand displacement, so it is recorded as non_conformant rather than dismissed as noise.

payload.reason: Confirm executor's failure claim: check whether line_green is actually seated at its placement frame

payload.explanation: The executor's own end_step claim for place_line_green reported claimed_outcome=failure, with position_error_m 0.0218 (> tolerance 0.015) and orientation_mismatch_deg_estimate ">80", plus a visual_confirmation note that line_green was "lying flat near the slot, not seated in it". Independent query_snapshot confirms and sharpens this: line_green at (0.3978,-0.2078,0.0733) vs line_green_placement at (0.3954,-0.2044,0.0524), a 0.0474 m departure -- over three times the 0.015 m position tolerance -- with orientation (0.0199,-0.6526,0.0046,0.7574) wildly different from the placement frame's near-identity orientation, consistent with the part having toppled onto its side rather than seated upright. look() confirms the gripper is withdrawn and line_green is visibly off the slot. This corroborates the mechanism inferred from the two invariant findings already recorded in this step (clamp-effort spike to 191 and a 0.0213 m in-hand slip, both during the final lowering into the base1 slot): line_green met resistance going into the slot, shifted in the gripper under the reaction force, and was released in a toppled, grossly misseated pose rather than properly inserted. The grasp/lift effects from the pick phase (lift height 0.3 m, grasp width error 0.0042 m, effort plateau 11.86) were clean and are not in question; the failure is specific to the seating outcome. u_brown and u_orange shifted by 0.0085 m and 0.009 m respectively during this episode, both within their 0.02 m disturbance tolerance, so they are not separately flagged. The executor's retry is already underway (observed step_id pick_line_green_retry), so this finding covers the failed first attempt at place_line_green; its outcome will be reassessed against whatever step re-seats line_green.

payload.explanation: This is the run's final end-state verdict. u_brown and u_orange: both independently re-measured at run end against their (base1-relative) placement frames -- u_brown 0.0021 m off, u_orange 0.0023 m off, both well within tolerance, confirming the executor's success claims. line_green: non_conformant. Its place_line_green attempt was already flagged twice as a finding (clamp effort 191.19 vs 170 tolerated, and a 0.0213 m in-hand slip, both while the part met resistance seating into the base1 slot) and a third finding at that step's own end_step (part toppled, 0.0474 m / >80 deg off its placement frame). The executor itself then reported claimed_outcome=failure and attempted recovery: pick_line_green_retry succeeded cleanly but IK/orientation repeatedly failed to re-seat it (execute_approach_and_preposition failing four times across retries), a reset_line_green intermediate rest was clean and did not disturb any other object, and a final pick_line_green_retry2 attempt produced a grasp whose measured width (0.0407 m) did not match the authored 0.03 m; the executor opened the gripper and aborted (phase regrasped_aborting) rather than claim a mismatched grasp as success -- this is the correct behavior under the missed-grasp requirement, so no finding is recorded against it. One monitor fire during this abort (slip_line_green3, 0.0238 m) was a mis-arming: get_evidence on finger_joint shows the gripper already opening (effort falling to ~0) before the fire, i.e. it fired on the deliberate release, not on a held part slipping; no verdict was recorded for it. The run then ended with status=aborted. Critically, the executor's own run_ended detail claims "line_green currently grasped in gripper," but my own query_snapshot at finalization shows finger_joint fully open (0.4365 rad, ~0 effort) and line_green resting on the bench at (0.704,-0.289,0.018), 0.87 m from the TCP (0.873,-0.514,0.395) -- the part is plainly not held. This is exactly the disagreement this record exists to capture: executor claims a grasp that the physical evidence contradicts. line_green's final position is 0.32 m from line_green_placement, grossly outside its 0.015 m tolerance -- a standing, uncorrected violation. inverted_u_yellow was never touched (still at its original rest pose); since no place step for it ever opened, this is accounted for as unattempted, not as a separate non-conformance. All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) are confirmed via query_snapshot to be at their exact original poses, undisturbed throughout. base1 is confirmed within 0.00406 m of its arm-time reference, well inside the 0.02 m tolerance used for it (an agent-chosen value by analogy to the registry's disturbance_tolerance_m, since base1 carries no object contract of its own) -- undisturbed. Three unplanned steps occurred (pick_line_green_retry, reset_line_green, pick_line_green_retry2); none violated any standing requirement and all are named here as unplanned per protocol. Because a violation (line_green's grossly misseated final pose) stands uncorrected at run end, the verdict is non_conformant: this outranks "incomplete" even though the executor stopped before reaching inverted_u_yellow, and it holds regardless of the executor's own "aborted" framing.
